Box 12.2 Success story: Calcutta Leather Complex in Bantala
The Calcutta Leather Complex in Bantala was developed by the State Government to facilitate the shifting of all tanneries operating
in Tangra, Topsia and Tiljala in Kolkata in compliance of the order of the Hon’ble Supreme Court. The Complex, developed over
1,100 acres, started operation in 2005. It now has 326 tanneries (245 shifted from Kolkata and 81 new). The total wastewater
generation is estimated to be 19.91 MLD and this is treated in a Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) of capacity 20 MLD (4
modules each of capacity 5 MLD). The Government has taken the initiative to add two more modules each of capacity 5 MLD to
ensure treatment of effluent to be generated by upcoming tanneries in the Complex. The CETP in the Calcutta Leather Complex is an
example of how small and medium industries can benefit from such common facilities.
